# Affine corrections and the three-fiber local polygonization theorem

This extends `candidate ccc70a2b68222695`.
All conclusions are local on a normal interval of length less than pi with
uniformly positive C2 curvature and constant, separated cap memberships.
No assertion about global cap crossings or zero-curvature sets is made.

## 1. Affine corrections preserve every Jensen inequality

For a finite base P subset R^n put e(z)=(1,z_1,...,z_n). Use the residual
support functions f_z=h_z-B_z, the common nodal projection F_z=P_delta f_z,
and the positive interval energy Q from the preceding note.

Suppose the vectors

    u_z=e(z) tensor f_z

are linearly independent in the Hilbert direct sum of n+1 copies of
H_0^1(I). Then their projected Gram matrix

    A_zw=(e(z) dot e(w)) Q(F_z,F_w)

is positive definite for all sufficiently fine meshes, with uniformly
bounded inverse. Let d_z=Q(f_z-F_z,f_z-F_z)/2=O(delta^2).

Choose corrections

    psi_z=sum_w xi_w (e(z) dot e(w)) F_w.

The map z -> psi_z is affine. It therefore cancels from every Jensen
support difference. Common-normal interpolation already preserves those
differences by its positive sine coefficients. There is no contact-pattern
or support-gap assumption in this argument.

The fiber-area corrections are exactly

    -(A xi)_z-q_z(xi),      q_z(xi)=Q(psi_z,psi_z)/2.

Thus solve A xi+q(xi)=d. On a ball of radius R delta^2, the map
xi -> A^(-1)(d-q(xi)) maps that ball into itself for sufficiently large fixed
R and sufficiently small delta, and has Lipschitz constant O(delta^2)<1.
Indeed A^(-1) is uniformly bounded, d=O(delta^2), q=O(||xi||^2), and its
bilinear coefficients are uniformly bounded. The contraction iteration
therefore converges to an exact solution xi=O(delta^2).

The correction changes interior curvature atoms by O(delta^3) and endpoint
atoms by O(delta^2), dominated by the original positive O(delta) margins.
All fiber areas and all fixed cap areas are restored exactly, while the
supports outside I are unchanged.

## 2. The only three-collinear-fiber rank failure is homothety

For z=-1,0,1, a dependence of the tensor vectors gives

    lambda_- f_- +lambda_0 f_0+lambda_+ f_+=0,
    -lambda_- f_-+lambda_+ f_+=0.

Every f_z is strictly negative in int(I): it has zero endpoint values and
f_z''+f_z>0, so the positive Dirichlet Green kernel gives this sign.
In a nonzero dependence none of the three lambda's can vanish. The equations
therefore force all f_z to be positive scalar multiples of one function f.
The same argument works for any three distinct collinear base indices.
For three affinely independent indices the tensor vectors are automatically
independent, by applying affine coordinate functionals separating the indices.

## 3. The rank-one residual case admits an exact local correction

Suppose f_z=c_z f with c_z>0. In any finite Jensen support inequality its
gap has the form

    g=D+kappa f >=0,      D''+D=0,      f''+f=r>0.

A nonidentity gap has at most one zero in the INTERIOR of I. Endpoint
zeros need not obey this count. To see this:

* If kappa<0, an interior zero is a local minimum, so g''>=0 there,
  contradicting g''+g=kappa r<0.
* If kappa=0, an interior zero and its zero derivative force the homogeneous
  ODE solution to vanish identically. Otherwise there is no interior zero.
* If kappa>0, two zeros at u<v, with v-u<pi, would give a function satisfying
  g''+g>0 and zero endpoints. The positive Dirichlet Green kernel for
  -d^2/dtheta^2-1 forces g<0 between them, a contradiction.

A finite base has only finitely many extreme barycentric representations:
each representation set is a bounded polytope defined by finitely many linear
constraints. It suffices to enforce their finitely many Jensen inequalities.
Consequently there is a compact subinterval J inside I on which every
nonidentity gap is strictly positive. Identity gaps have D=kappa=0 and are
preserved by every common base-function replacement.

Begin with common-normal interpolation h_z^mesh=B_z+c_z F, F=P_delta f.
It preserves all gaps everywhere. Choose a nonzero smooth phi<=0 compactly
supported in J, and put Phi=P_delta phi. For fine meshes its support remains
in J and

    A=Q(F,Phi) -> Q(f,phi)=-integral r phi>0,
    B=Q(Phi,Phi)>0,
    E=Q(f-F,f-F)=O(delta^2).

Choose

    xi=E/[A+sqrt(A^2+B E)].

Then 2A xi+B xi^2=E and xi=O(delta^2), so replacing F by F+xi Phi restores
its Q norm exactly. Every fiber norm, and hence its area, is also restored
because its residual is c_z times that common function. Corrections are
supported in J and are uniformly O(delta^2); its positive gaps remain
positive. Outside J the valid interpolated gaps are unchanged. The curvature
atom estimates again guarantee convexity.

This proves the rank-one case without assuming a globally stable contact
pattern on I.

## 4. Combined local result for at most three fibers

For any compatible family of at most three positive planar fibers, with
uniform positive C2 curvature on I and separated constant cap memberships,
all their arcs over I admit simultaneous exact polygonization preserving all
areas, cap areas, outside supports, and every support compatibility relation.

For three collinear indices use Section 1 unless the tensor vectors are
dependent, in which case Sections 2 and 3 apply. For affinely independent
indices use Section 1 directly. The one- and two-fiber cases are immediate
from tensor independence.

The result is local. It does not automatically polygonize portions containing
cap-crossing points, arbitrary curvature degeneracies, or a full boundary in
one step. Those are separate obligations.
